Container.Name: tesla-drive
Container.Overview: YouTube in the Tesla browser while the car is in Drive, for passengers. Tesla pauses ordinary video elements at the OS level in Drive, so this app never uses one: a small home server resolves YouTube streams with yt-dlp, transcodes video to MPEG1-TS with ffmpeg, streams it over a WebSocket, and the web page decodes it in JavaScript/WebGL (JSMpeg) onto a canvas. Audio travels as a separate MP3 stream. One container serves the YouTube-style front page, the search/trending APIs and the WebSocket on a single port. PASSENGER USE ONLY while the car is moving — the driver must never watch or interact with it, and you are responsible for your local laws. Do not expose this to the public internet without authentication; keep it on your LAN or reach it over Tailscale / a reverse proxy with auth.

Config.Name: WebUI and API Port
Config.Description: The single port for the web front page, JSON APIs and the MPEG1 WebSocket (same origin).

Config.Name: Config Directory
Config.Description: Appdata folder. Optionally holds cookies.txt (Netscape format, exported from a browser signed in to YouTube) for when YouTube bot-blocks your IP. See config/cookies.txt.example in the repo.

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: Port the app listens on inside the container.

Config.Name: Bind Host
Config.Description: Bind address inside the container. Keep 0.0.0.0 for Docker/Unraid (the port mapping controls exposure); bare-metal local use defaults to 127.0.0.1.

Config.Name: yt-dlp Cookies File
Config.Description: Optional. Path (inside the container) to a Netscape cookies.txt for yt-dlp. Only used when the file exists; leave as-is if you do not use cookies.
